status: Code, static call-path review and metadata only. No Java, Gradle, unit/GameTest, game, native binary or media execution.
scope: Player-reported Blackwatch corpse hopping; passive generic corpse constraint response, also applicable to the same renderer used by other dead actors.
evidence: Part.step applies gravity to every limb on every half-step. Only that limb own translation collision previously removed downward velocity and advanced still.

Joint.solve and the final connectedPose positional projection restore the connected skeleton after integration without changing the retained velocity. A head/forearm held above terrain can accumulate downward speed while repeatedly being put back by its parent.
The old allMatch(still>=24) corpse sleep gate additionally required every limb to collide downward by itself; a supported torso with suspended connected limbs could never satisfy it.
The same mismatch exists for stored spin when the final joint angle correction rejects the integrated orientation. A positional repair is not a fresh impulse.

CorpseFragmentMotion.drop is an absolute elapsed-time parabola with a ground clamp, used by ConsumeFracture cosmetic fragments; no repeated accumulator was found there, and that helper was not changed.
changes: Retain each corpse part half-step initial and unconstrained final pose. After existing joint/terrain/connected-skin projection, reject only velocity directed opposite the actual constraint correction. Do not derive velocity from terrain lift or joint-repair displacement.
Apply the corresponding shortest-rotation correction to world angular velocity, then express remaining spin in the corrected local frame.
Count rest using remaining velocity/spin and completed position/orientation displacement, with the existing0.002 speed-square and24half-step criteria.
Require real downward collision support within0.025blocks, propagated only along surviving joints. Reuse Entity.collideBoundingBox and the existing bounded9-probe path for very large parts.
Recheck sleeping component support each tick. Removing its ground resets its rest state; detached unsupported fragments cannot inherit support across a cut.
New response runs only for dead, uncaptured bodies. Live recovery/consume pull paths, gravity, restitution, mass, rig and cut budgets are unchanged this batch.

mathBoundary.linear: For correction c with v dot c<0, vNew=v-c*(v dot c)/(c dot c). Squared speed decreases by (v dot c)^2/(c dot c); other motion is unchanged. Corrections shorter than existing1e-5 collision epsilon are ignored.
mathBoundary.angular: Use the vector axis of shortest correctedRotation*inverse(predictedRotation), apply the same projection in world space and rotate back. Unit quaternion rotations preserve speed norm, up to float rounding.
mathBoundary.limit: This is a dissipative MC solver correction, not a claim of exact P1 rigid-body physics or conservation of full linked-body momentum. No restitution/friction constants were tuned.

runner: Existing tools/player-fix-unit.init.gradle includes **/Ragdoll*Test.class; playerFixUnit serial queue requires no change.
previousCutWork: The already recorded13anatomical-joint soldier grouping,48intact+16fragment reserve and merged Part collider/center/inertia rebuild remain in place. No additional accepted sharp-cut failure was statically proved in this batch.

Check living knockdown/getup and active consume visuals remain unaffected. This change does not add dead-corpse grabbing.
No claim that the player-visible fish-like hopping is eliminated until normal-client verification.
